guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is low, key_dec_q is cleared to all zeros asynchronously.
On each posedge clk_i when key_dec_we == SP2V_HIGH, key_dec_q is updated with key_dec_d.
When not reset and key_dec_we != SP2V_HIGH, key_dec_q retains its previous value (no update).

assumptions.claim: SP2V_HIGH represents a valid write-enable level (e.g., 1'b1) and is driven consistently elsewhere.
assumptions.risk: If SP2V_HIGH is not a stable valid value, key_dec_q may never update or update continuously, corrupting the key.

assumptions.claim: key_dec_d is valid and stable at least a hold time after the posedge clk_i when key_dec_we == SP2V_HIGH.
assumptions.risk: Incorrect or metastable key value captured into key_dec_q, leading to wrong decryption outputs.

assumptions.claim: rst_ni is asserted (low) before the key is used to ensure known initial state (all zeros).
assumptions.risk: If reset is not applied, key_dec_q may contain unknown (X) values in simulation or unpredictable bits in hardware, potentially causing secret leakage or malfunction.

uncertain_points.claim: key_dec_q reset to all zeros provides a known key (all zeros) that could be used inadvertently if the decrypt data path starts before a proper key is loaded. There is no explicit key_valid gating in this register chunk.
uncertain_points.cond: After reset, if key_dec_q holds zero and a decryption operation is triggered before key load completes, the zero key will be used.
uncertain_points.risk: Potential plaintext exposure if decryption with zero key occurs, especially if the core is accessible after reset without key provisioning verification.
